_fixture: ISS-1060 · what a resident master's Claude Code conversation records when its account refuses a turn, and when it does not

_captured.how: one line taken verbatim per distinct (apiErrorStatus, error, quotaLimits.rateLimitType) shape observed on the box, plus the smallest successful assistant turn and one record carrying the refusal banner only inside its text

_constructed.why: no box has produced these two, so they are written rather than captured, and saying otherwise would be a lie. They are the counterexamples the classifier must refuse, not evidence of anything Claude Code does.

=========== ISS-1060
{
  "documentId": "b3452d86-e105-4d40-b2b5-452a427ed20d",
  "issueId": "ISS-1060",
  "title": "A capped Claude account reaches core, so the fleet stops prompting masters into a wall it cannot see",
  "description": "## What happened

The fleet keeps prompting resident masters into a Claude account that has already refused, because
nothing tells core the account is capped.

Measured on `forge-vm`, 2026-09-16 10:28Z. The forge-dev master pane had printed:

```
You've hit your session limit · resets 8:30pm (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh)
Opus 5 │ 5h:██████████ 101% │ 7d:██░░░░░░░░ 28%
```

Five of the six live masters on the box had hit the same wall — forge-dev, sid-desk, sidpeak,
mowment and codemap; only pixelight had not. At that same moment the runner row in core read:

```
forge-vm   status: online   limitReason: null   rateLimitedUntil: null   limitDetail: null
```

So the box went on sweeping at its normal interval and prompting each master on the normal refresh
period, and every one of those prompts is a full agent pass spent against a cap. The backoff that
exists for exactly this case never engaged, because it keys on a runner row that nothing had
stamped.

## Why it happens

Core already has the receiving half, written for this exact case. `devices/master-limit.ts` states
the gap in its own header:

> A resident master is on neither [the job lane nor the chat lane]: it produces no job of its own
> and no chat session, so when its Claude account hits a cap the fact reached nothing —
> `detect_usage_limit` has exactly one caller in the runner, on the stream-json branch a master
> does not use.

`POST /me/limit` is mounted in `devices/pool-routes.ts` and calls `recordMasterLimit` /
`clearMasterLimit`, which stamp and clear the same runner columns the job lane uses. Searching the
runner crates for `master-limit`, `master_limit` or any call to that route returns nothing. The
producer was never written.

This is the same shape as ISS-1050: a consumer wired and correct, a producer that does not exist,
and a mechanism that reads as working because nothing reports its silence.

## Where

`packages/runner/crates/forge-runner-core` (the daemon that owns the pane and reads its output) and
`packages/core/src/devices/master-limit.ts` + `pool-routes.ts` (already built, already mounted).

## Outcome

When a resident master's account refuses a turn for a usage or rate cap, the box says so, core
records it against that runner, and the fleet stops spending passes into the wall until the window
resets or the cap is cleared. An operator reading the runner sees why the box went quiet, instead
of seeing a healthy row and an idle fleet.

## Rules

**The report comes from the thing that saw the refusal.** The pane is where the cap is stated, so
the daemon that owns the pane is what reports it. Do not infer a cap from silence, from a pane's
byte count, or from a turn taking a long time — those are the inferences this repo has already
removed once.

**Both directions, or neither.** The stamp makes the cap visible; the clear ends the window when a
turn succeeds again. A stamp with no clear leaves a box that an operator has already fixed looking
capped until a parsed reset time that may be wrong, and the reset is a guess about a fact that can
change the moment an account is swapped.

**A cap is not a fault.** It must not quarantine the box, must not retire the runner, and must not
move any issue. Work already running continues; only the starting of new turns backs off.

**Backing off is not stopping.** Whatever interval the capped state selects, the box must keep
checking, because the clear can only be observed by trying. A state that stops trying cannot
self-heal, and an operator who fixes the account out of band would be left watching an idle fleet.

**Prove it with a refusal that really happened.** Plant a cap the box can actually read — or replay
a captured refusal — and watch the runner row gain its reason, the interval widen, and both go back
after a success. A test that asserts the stamp without a refusal reaching it proves nothing.

## Out of scope

- Raising, buying or managing account quota.
- The `forge-plugin` repository.
- Anything about how masters are dispatched, what they may claim, or the admissible set.
- The job lane and the chat lane, which already report caps through their own paths and are not
  changed here.",
